sense: be about to happen: of danger, of a storm

terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, intransitive: with the dative or in + accusative
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 31: licet undique omnēs in mē terrōrēs impendeant (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly, to hang over (a rock, a sword: Cic. Tusc. 5.62); of dangers and troubles, to threaten.

terms.gloss: loom over; be close at hand
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, intransitive, with the dative
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.91: mors … cotīdiē imminet (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly, to overhang or rise above (a hill over a town, Verg. A. 1.420); then of what is near and threatening: death, danger, war. Of a person, it also means to be eager for something (Cic. Phil. 5.20).

evidence: Cic. Planc. 95: dēflagrātiōnem urbī minābātur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of things as well as people: a house on fire “threatened the city with burning” (Cic. Planc. 95).

phrases.english: The clouds look threatening; let’s hurry home.

sources: Lewis & Short: impendeo · Lewis & Short: immineo · Lewis & Short: minor
